title: Probability is Not Enough: Exploring and Counting Divergent Tokens for Reasoning Uncertainty Quantification in LLMs
abstract: arXiv:2609.38070v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: As the chain-of-thought reasoning capabilities of large language models improve, evaluating and calibrating their reasoning confidence is becoming increasingly important for quantifying the uncertainty of their answers. Current methods for estimating the confidence of large language models are generally based on probabilities of selected key tokens, but the underlying mechanism remains unclear. Our pilot study finds that replacing selected token probabilities with coarse substitutes can also improve calibration, motivating us to further explore effective signals of model confidence. We introduce Divergent Token Confidence (DTC), a framework that estimates confidence by counting tokens at which two models strongly disagree during decoding. DTC identifies these divergent tokens using the Jensen-Shannon divergence between next-token distributions evaluated along the same reasoning trajectory. translated_title: 概率并不足够：探索并计数发散标记以实现大语言模型推理的不确定性量化
translated_abstract: 随着大语言模型思维链推理能力的提升，评估和校准其推理置信度对于量化答案的不确定性变得越来越重要。目前估计大语言模型置信度的方法通常基于所选关键标记的概率，但其底层机制仍不清楚。我们的初步研究发现，用粗略的替代信号替换所选标记概率同样能够改善校准效果，这促使我们进一步探索模型置信度的有效信号。我们提出了发散标记置信度框架，该框架通过统计两个模型在解码过程中产生强烈分歧的标记数量来估计置信度。DTC利用在同一推理轨迹上评估的下一标记分布之间的Jensen-Shannon散度来识别这些发散标记。我们发现发散标记的数量与置信度几乎呈负相关……
tldr: 该论文提出发散标记置信度（DTC）框架，通过利用Jensen-Shannon散度统计两个模型在同一推理轨迹上产生强烈分歧的标记数量来估计大语言模型推理的置信度，为不确定性量化提供了比标记概率更有效的信号。
en_tdlr: This paper introduces Divergent Token Confidence (DTC), a framework that estimates LLM reasoning confidence by counting divergent tokens—identified via Jensen-Shannon divergence between next-token distributions along the same reasoning trajectory—providing a more effective signal for uncertainty quantification than token probabilities alone.
